brief: The sky and the ground ignore each other. drawClouds() draws eleven hashed banks on a (simT + windX) drift, but it draws them in the SKY STRIP only - above hz, under the backdrop - and nothing they pass over is shaded: the town has no moving cloud shadow. shadowF()/shSpread()/shOffset() only soften every object's own shadow uniformly under a lid. Connect them: let the banks throw soft shadows that travel across the courtyard, the allotments, the plaza and the river with the wind, so that on a broken-cloud day the light MOVES over the town and a viewer sees weather passing rather than a dimmer switch. The wide shot is where this pays: it is the only change on this list that alters the whole picture at once.
measured: Not measured, deliberately - I am not going to invent a coverage target. Grepped and confirmed on HEAD: `cloudShadow` and `shadeAt` do not exist; drawClouds' only geometry is at `hz`; shadowF() has 14 call sites and every one is an object's own shadow. Pick the intensity by looking at it, and report what you chose.
successLooksLike: On a seed and day with cloudCover in the broken band, a filmstrip cropped to the courtyard lawn shows the light rising and falling as a bank crosses, and the same instants at cloudCover < 0.04 are IDENTICAL to HEAD. The shadow travels with windDir() and reverses with windSign.
avoid: Deterministic only - hash and simT, no new R() draw. This is a live pass, not a cache rebuild: the ground cache is repainted on its own dirty flag and a per-frame truth on it belongs in a live overlay (drawLitPanes' idiom). Watch the frame cost - `frame-cost.mjs`, not `perf.mjs` - a full-frame per-pixel pass will not do; a handful of soft ellipses composited in one multiply will.
